messages:
alex: Noticed a new perf wobble in the nightly integration run. p95 decode jumps ~25% after kernel-fingerprint scheduling change.
jin: Seen it too. The tracer points to heavy time in host::frame_assembler + repeated small writev syscalls.
maria: Any change in kvcache metrics?
alex: Yes  kvcache eviction rate doubled briefly, hit-rate down ~7%. This coincides with more fragmented host frames being parsed.
sam: We recently changed kernel selection to favor smallest-macros for <40 token sequences which increased number of kernel switches. Could be write amplification.
dave: I pulled a sample flamegraph: https://perf.redwood/trace/def456. Hotspots: frame_assembler::append_fragment, net::grpc_writev, kv_cache::shrink_on_insert.
jin: Hypothesis: smaller kernels -> more, smaller output chunks -> host reassembly runs more often -> more tiny writes -> more kvcache churn because prefixes aren't kept warm long enough.
maria: Mitigation ideas: 1) delayed-commit coalesce on host egress (configurable window, default 750us) 2) extend parse reassembly window to accept slightly larger fragments before chopping 3) affinity-based batching: group requests by kernel_fingerprint + recent-kv-access to keep locality.
alex: Delayed-commit sketch:
```
// host/egress/coalesce.h
struct CoalesceWindow { uint32_t max_bytes = 4096; uint32_t window_us = 750; };
if (pending_bytes < max_bytes && head_age < window_us) merge_and_defer_write(); else flush();
```
sam: For affinity batching we can add a short buffer that groups requests into same kernel_fingerprint if they arrive within 1ms and seq_len within +/- 12. That avoids flips.
dave: Also tune kvcache eviction policy: change min_eviction_size from 1% -> 4% so we evict more meaningfully instead of many tiny evictions.
jin: Low-risk canary plan: enable delayed-commit + affinity-bucket on a single pool, kv.min_eviction=4%. Run the standard mixed-user synthetic for 30m. Monitor p50/p95 decode, kvcache hit-rate, net.writev_syscalls/sec.
maria: I'll add alerts: rollback if kv hit-rate drops >1.5% or p95 increases >12% for more than 5m.
perf-bot: Canary job created: https://perf.redwood/job/1747659999-canary (queued).
-- 20m later --
alex: Canary summary vs baseline: p50 36ms -> 33ms (-8%), p95 210ms -> 165ms (-21%), kvcache hit-rate 87.2% -> 91.5%, writev syscalls/sec 9.2k -> 2.7k.
dave: Nice. Also observed CPU drop in parse_assembler stack traces.
sam: No regressions seen for long sequences; kernel affinity keeps large sequences on big kernels.
jin: Opened PR with changes + config flags: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/6342. Defaults: coalesce_window_us=750, max_coalesce_bytes=4096, affinity_ms=1, seq_len_delta=12, kv.min_eviction_pct=4.
alex: Let's roll canary to 5% traffic and watch for 1h, then increment. Rollback plan ready.
maria: I'll schedule the 5% ramp at 23:30 UTC. Posting updates in #eng-runtime after each step. :rocket:
perf-bot: Canary scheduled: 1747662000.
thread_text: host-side delayed-commit coalesce + affinity batching to cut write amplification and kvcache thrash after kernel-fingerprint scheduling
